title: In Leviticus 22 In What Ways Can We Ensure That Our Worship Is Acceptable To God
paragraphs: Acceptable Worship: Insights from Leviticus 22

Leviticus 22 offers a detailed glimpse into the standards God set for Old Testament priests and the people regarding acceptable worship. While these instructions were given to Israel, they also reveal enduring principles about approaching God that remain relevant for believers today. This study will explore practical ways we can ensure our worship is pleasing to God, drawing both from Leviticus 22 and the broader testimony of Scripture.
1. Approaching God with Reverence and Purity
Leviticus 22 emphasizes that those who draw near to God must do so with reverence and moral cleanliness. Priests were required to avoid ceremonial uncleanness when offering sacrifices:

Say unto them, Whosoever he be of all your seed throughout your generations, that approacheth unto the holy things, which the children of Israel hallow unto Jehovah, having his uncleanness upon him, that soul shall be cut off from before me: I am Jehovah. -
Leviticus 22:3 ASV

This principle translates to a call for believers today to approach God with a heart cleansed by faith in Christ. While ritual purity is no longer required, inward holiness and sincerity are essential.
If we confess our sins, he is faithful and righteous to forgive us our sins, and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness. -
1 John 1:9 ASV
2. Offering Our Best to God
Leviticus 22 repeatedly instructs Israel not to offer animals with blemishes. God deserves our best, not what is leftover or inferior:
But whatsoever hath a blemish, that shall ye not offer: for it shall not be acceptable for you. -
Leviticus 22:20 ASV
Today, this principle challenges us to give God first place in our time, talents, resources, and devotion. Worship becomes unacceptable when it is offered carelessly or half-heartedly.
Whether therefore ye eat, or drink, or whatsoever ye do, do all to the glory of God. -
1 Corinthians 10:31 ASV
3. Worship Rooted in Obedience and Faith
Obedience is central to worship. God’s instructions in Leviticus 22 were not suggestions, but requirements for acceptable worship. Jesus affirms this principle:
But the hour cometh, and now is, when the true worshippers shall worship the Father in spirit and truth: for such doth the Father seek to be his worshippers. -
John 4:23 ASV
True worship is not just outward form, but an obedient heart aligned with God’s truth, made possible through faith in Christ.
And without faith it is impossible to be well-pleasing unto him; for he that cometh to God must believe that he is, and that he is a rewarder of them that seek after him. -
Hebrews 11:6 ASV
4. Worship Offered Through Christ Alone
While Leviticus 22 centers on the priestly system, the New Testament reveals that Jesus is our perfect High Priest and sacrifice. Our worship is acceptable only through Him:
By him therefore let us offer up a sacrifice of praise to God continually, that is, the fruit of lips which make confession to his name. -
Hebrews 13:15 ASV
We approach God not on the basis of our own merit, but through the finished work of Christ, who makes us acceptable before God.
For through him we both have our access in one Spirit unto the Father. -
Ephesians 2:18 ASV
Conclusion

Leviticus 22 reminds us that God cares deeply about how we approach Him. Acceptable worship involves reverence, offering our best, obedience to His Word, and coming through Jesus Christ alone. May our worship reflect hearts transformed by grace, seeking to honor God in all we do.
